newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Chretien evasive on Martin's future.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Chretien evasive on Martin's future.

text.p: Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien was evasive on Wednesday about whether Paul Martin would remain as finance minister.
Asked to reassure the markets that Martin would stay on, Chretien told Reuters: "You know, he is the minister of finance. So if I make any change it will be known next week."
Pressed to confirm if was likely Martin would keep his portfolio, Chretien declined to respond as he walked to his office from a news conference.
During the news conference he announced that he would swear in his new cabinet next Wednesday, followed by a two-day planning session.

Chretien, whose Liberal government was re-elected on Monday with a reduced majority, indicated throughout the campaign that Martin, who won international credibility for tough budget deficit cutting, would continue in his post.
Chretien spokesman Peter Donolo said on Tuesday that he could not see any reason that Chretien would remove Martin.
